channel.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
channel.description: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

item.title: Five arrested near UK air base used by U.S. bombers in Iran war
item.description: U.K. police say five men were arrested on suspicion of preparation of a terrorist act after three vehicles were spotted near an air base the U.S. military has been using to launch attacks on Iran.
item.content:encoded: U.K. police say five men were arrested on suspicion of preparation of a terrorist act after three vehicles were spotted near an air base the U.S. military has been using to launch attacks on Iran.

item.title: After more than two decades, U.S. forces prepare to leave Iraq
item.description: The U.S. military formally ends a more than two-decade-long presence in Iraq this week.
item.content:encoded: The U.S. military formally ends a more than two-decade-long presence in Iraq this week.

item.title: Fall planting isn't over. Try greens, garlic or both
item.description: A University of Maryland farm manager explains why Swiss chard and garlic are good choices for a home garden this fall.

item.title: The L.A. fires gave new life to a composer's firefighter anthem
item.description: LA-based composer Charles-Henri Avelange wrote a score to honor firefighters almost 20 years ago. After last year's wildfires in Los Angeles, he's made headway in finally recording it.

item.title: Laleh Khadivi's new novel asks how well we know our mothers
item.description: In Laleh Khadivi's new novel "Female Life on Planet Earth", a woman finds photographs that reveal unknown layers of her late mother's past.

item.title: We're looking for life on other planets. Are we ready to find it?
item.description: In 1960, astronomer Frank Drake listened for signals from alien worlds. Reporter Brendan Byrne's podcast When We Find Them picks up the search and asks what would happen if we finally find something.

item.title: Cineplexity: Blade Runner is a classic. Does that mean you have to like it?
item.description: What makes a movie a classic, and what if you just don't like it? Two NPR critics give their honest opinions.

item.title: CNN is getting new owners with close ties to Trump
item.description: Two big TV news outlets, CBS and CNN, will now be controlled by Trump allies. Some journalists are worried about pressure on their coverage.

item.title: Trump gave Xi Jinping a warm welcome. What did the talks accomplish?
item.description: From the National Archives to the state dinner, President Trump and Xi Jinping looked comfortable together in Washington. Two former NPR China correspondents on what the visit did and didn't deliver.

item.title: At the Smithsonian, Maya Angelou's typewriter holds a place of honor
item.description: A typewriter Maya Angelou used for decades is on display at the Smithsonian's National Museum of American History, near the original Star-Spangled Banner. A curator explains why it belongs there.
